evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.85, TOP reaction arrow, labelled with the italic 'i' (inductive cleavage). The drawn reactant is protonated methyl isopropyl ether, written on the page as (CH3)2CH-O(+)(H)-CH3 with the '+' printed on the OXYGEN and the O-bound H drawn explicitly; the mapped SMILES localizes the charge on that same oxygen (convention B). The drawn products are 'i-C3H7+ + CH3OH' with '40%' printed underneath. MECHANISM: heterolysis of the C1-O4 bond with both electrons going to the oxygen, which leaves as neutral methanol and leaves the even-electron isopropyl cation (m/z 43.0542, curator-computed monoisotopic). Book draws 0 arc(s): Equation 8.85 contains NO curved electron-pushing arrows at all - it is drawn with straight reaction/equilibrium arrows plus dashed 'partial bond' strokes that denote the loose bonds of the ion-neutral complexes. The single encoded move <1> is reconstructed for electron balance (not drawn on the page). NOTE ON THE DRAWN INTERMEDIATE: the vertical double arrow below the reactant leads to the same dissociation drawn as an ion-neutral COMPLEX 'CH2(H)-CH(CH3)...O(+)(H)CH3' (a dashed C...O bond, one methyl H drawn out explicitly because it is the H that becomes labile); that complex is non-covalent and has no defined bond orders, so it is not encoded as a discrete mapped species - this record encodes the net C-O heterolysis, which is what the dashed bond depicts. The up-arrow at the centre of the scheme shows that the same 40% products are also reached from the proton-bound complex of Equation 8.85b. CONTEXT: the p.199 text introduces Equation 8.85 with 'In the absence of activating functional groups in EE ions, proton-exchange reactions can proceed in ion-molecule complexes (Equations 8.14, 8.85; Terlouw et al. 1986; Bowen 1991); demonstration of such pathways usually requires D-labeling. Here both the hydrogen lability and site receptivity' [continues on p.200] 'are determined by the relative proton affinities of the donor and acceptor sites: PA(C3H6, CH3OH) = 7.8, 7.9 eV. Note that the competitive dissociations of such a proton-bound isomer of (AB + H)+ produce AH+ and BH+, whose mass sum equals AB + 2.' The reacting ion is therefore the protonated molecule (AB+H)+ of methyl isopropyl ether, C4H11O+, curator-computed monoisotopic m/z 75.0804; the page prints no m/z for it. The two percentages printed on the page (40%, 60%) are the BRANCHING abundances of the two competing dissociation channels, not 70 eV EI relative intensities.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.85, so no MØD rule is cross-linked. Candidates checked and REJECTED: IMS_8_10 ('[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11)>>...[C+]5....[O]8{=}[C]9...') and IMS_8_12 both require an OXOCARBENIUM precursor - the left side pins a DOUBLE bond [O+]8{=}[C]9 - whereas Equation 8.85 starts from a protonated ether whose O+ carries three single bonds (C, H, CH3); the pattern cannot match this substrate even though the bond that breaks (C-O, heterolytic, charge retained on carbon) is of the same inductive type. IMS_8_14_1/_1b (the proton-bound-complex rH pair) are additionally atom-unbalanced (their product half carries an extra methyl copy-pasted from IMS_8_13). The IMS_8_7_* 'hydrogen exchange in an ion-molecule complex' family operates on odd-electron ketone/enol systems, not on a protonated ether. Equation 8.85 is unmodelled by the current rule set.

The page prints '40%' under 'i-C3H7+ + CH3OH': that is the printed branching abundance of this channel relative to the competing 60% channel of Equation 8.85b, NOT a 70 eV EI relative intensity, and it is a channel yield rather than a measured peak height. relative_intensity 0.4 stores the printed percentage; observed_mz 43.0542 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of C3H7+ (electron-mass corrected) - the page prints no m/z.

ms_context.activation_method: unspecified - the page names no ionization or activation experiment; the reacting ion is the protonated molecule (AB+H)+ of methyl isopropyl ether discussed in the p.199/200 text (Terlouw et al. 1986; Bowen 1991). ionization_method 'CI' is the curator's inference for how an (AB+H)+ ion is made, NOT a statement printed on the page
